Altus Property Ventures, Inc. (APVI), formerly Altus San Nicolas Corp., was incorporated and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 28, 2007. The Company listed its shares of the Philippine Stock Exchange by way of introduction on June 26, 2020, transferring to the Main Board on May 13, 2022.The primary purpose of APVI is to engage in the business of selling, acquiring, building, constructing, developing, leasing and disposing of real estate properties and property development of all kinds and nature.

The Company owns and operates the North Wing of Robinsons Place Ilocos mall located at San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. The Company shall serve as a vehicle for possible future real estate ventures and opportunities.

Prior to December 20, 2019, APVI was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Robinsons Land Corporation (RLC) and an indirect subsidiary of JG Summit Holdings, Inc. (JGS) through RLC. On December 20, 2019, the Company became a direct subsidiary of JGS by virtue of the property dividend distribution by RLC to its stockholders.

Source: SEC Form 17-A (2024)

## Company: Altus Property Ventures, Inc. (APVI)
Sector: Property / Property
Altus Property Ventures, Inc. (APVI), formerly Altus San Nicolas Corp., was incorporated and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 28, 2007. The Company listed its shares of the Philippine Stock Exchange by way of introduction on June 26, 2020, transferring to the Main Board on May 13, 2022.The primary purpose of APVI is to engage in the business of selling, acquiring, building, constructing, developing, leasing and disposing of real estate properties and property development of all kinds and nature.

The Company owns and operates the North Wing of Robinsons Place Ilocos mall located at San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. The Company shall serve as a vehicle for possible future real estate ventures and opportunities.

Prior to December 20, 2019, APVI was a wholly-owned subsidiary of Robinsons Land Corporation (RLC) and an indirect subsidiary of JG Summit Holdings, Inc. (JGS) through RLC. On December 20, 2019, the Company became a direct subsidiary of JGS by virtue of the property dividend distribution by RLC to its stockholders.

storedThesis:
Altus Property Ventures is a single-asset holding company — it owns and operates the North Wing of Robinsons Place Ilocos, a regional mall in San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. The business is simple enough to understand: collect rental income from mall tenants, managed under the umbrella of the Gokongwei conglomerate through its parent JG Summit Holdings. That simplicity is a double-edged sword. A Rule #1 investor can model the cash flows clearly, but the absence of diversification means every risk is concentrated in one building in one province.

The moat here is narrow and borrowed rather than intrinsic. Robinsons Place Ilocos benefits from the Robinsons Land brand and the foot traffic that the broader mall ecosystem attracts, but APVI itself has no independent brand power, no proprietary tenant relationships, and no network effects. The switching cost for tenants is low — a competitor mall or even a commercial strip could lure them away. Regional malls in the Philippines face long-run structural headwinds from e-commerce penetration and shifting consumer behavior. The moat, such as it is, rests entirely on being the dominant enclosed mall in a secondary city, which is a defensible but fragile position.

Management quality is mixed. The Gokongwei group has a strong track record of capital discipline and operational competence across its portfolio companies, which provides a degree of institutional credibility. However, two issues give pause. The resignation in September 2025 of independent director Maynard Ngu — publicly linked to a DPWH flood control probe and allegations of being a political bagman — is not an operational risk per se, but it signals a governance gap in how independent directors were selected. More operationally concerning: 2026 Q1 results showed revenue down 24% and net income down 26% year-on-year, with no disclosed pipeline of new properties or expansion initiatives that would justify the company's existence as a separate listed entity. APVI declared a ₱1.30/share cash dividend in May 2026, signaling confidence in near-term cash generation, but this also implies management has no better use for the capital — i.e., no growth.

On valuation, the numbers look seductive at first glance: P/E of 6.9x, P/B of 0.9x, a PEG of 0.14x. But the 48% historical EPS growth figure is a statistical artifact of a low earnings base in early years after listing — 2025 earnings were essentially flat (+2%), and 2026 is tracking materially lower. The Rule #1 Sticker Price of ₱12.00 already sits above the current price of ₱10.74, meaning there is no margin of safety even at fair value. The MOS buy price of ₱6.00 requires a 44% decline from current levels. With decelerating earnings and a single-asset structure, the current price is not cheap — it is a value trap candidate.

Pass at ₱10.74. This is a small, illiquid, single-asset property vehicle with no identifiable growth engine, deteriorating 2026 top-line momentum, and a price that offers no margin of safety by Rule #1 standards. The Gokongwei pedigree and low P/B provide some floor, but a fair-value company with no moat and no growth is not a compelling long-term hold. Revisit only if price falls to the ₱6–₱7 range and management announces a credible second-asset pipeline.
